summary: Iteration 4 tested on the hosted preview with real Clerk ticket sign-ins for Alex (player) and Blair (admin). Covered: email preview, test email, challenges, rivalry (H2H) pages and the monthly digest preference. Backend: the new preview suite test_iteration4_challenges_emails_preview.py passes 16/16. The dev-header suite has 119 passed, 2 skipped. UI: every requested flow works end to end. Email preview iframe and meta work, and the member select changes the preview. Test email shows 'Test sent to blair+clerk_test@example.com.' and a second click shows 'Wait a minute before sending another test'. The Monthly tab shows the 'November 2026' subject, 0 opted-in recipients and hides the member select. The Challenges panel sits above the Fair match finder. Challenging player7 with a time and note shows 'Challenge sent · alerted in-app'; a duplicate shows 'You already have an open challenge with this player'; the challenger can cancel. Blair's notification 'Alex Tester challenged you' Open link goes to /me/matches?challenge=<id>, which gets the highlight class, and opponent Cancel is hidden while pending. Accept leads to the score form; Send score leads to 'Score Reported'. Alex then confirms in My results and the badge shows 'Rated'. The rivalry page is reachable from player-h2h-link, fair-match-h2h-player7 and challenge-h2h; it shows the score, 18 singles matches with deltas, and Doubles(0) is empty. The monthly-digest checkbox persists after a reload. At 390px there is no page-level overflow on /admin/members, /me/matches or the rivalry page. One real defect: the rivalry page score orientation is wrong.

minor.issue: score_text is returned in side_one orientation even when player A is on side two. A match Blair reported as 6-4 6-3 (Blair won) comes back with a_won=false and score '6-4 6-3', so the rivalry row reads 'Alex Tester 6-4 6-3 Blair Tester' with Blair as winner. Flip the score sets when a_side==2, either in the backend or in rivalry.tsx.
The challenge moves to 'completed' as soon as a score is reported. If the opponent then disputes or the result is voided, the challenge stays 'Score reported' with no way to report again or cancel.
Loads every finalized club match into memory and filters in Python, and calls club_ratings() 4 times per request. Filter in SQL and compute ratings once per kind.

ui_bugs.issue: Score is not flipped to player A's perspective (see backend minor #1), so the scoreline contradicts the bold winner

issues: Email HTML uses a fixed width=560 table, so in the 308px iframe the content is cut off and scrolls inside the frame. Use width=100% with max-width:560 for mobile email clients.
The Weekly recap / Monthly leaderboard tabs stack vertically and stretch full width on mobile
StatusBadge title-cases the text: 'Waiting For Reply', 'Accepted · Play And Report'
A player you already have an open challenge with still shows the Challenge button; the user only finds out from the 409 after submitting

action_items: Head-to-head: present score_text from player A's perspective (reverse each set when A is on side two) so the scoreline matches the winner
Handle a disputed or voided challenge result: let the challenge be reported again or cancelled
Make the email templates responsive (width=100%, max-width 560) so the mobile preview and mobile mail clients are not cut off
Optional: add data-testid to the 'Confirm result' and 'Dispute' buttons in ResultActions; mark an open challenge on fair-match rows
critical_code_review_comments: challenges.py create_challenge: the duplicate-open check is not atomic (race can create two open challenges). Add a partial unique index or lock.
challenges.py head_to_head: full-table scan of finalized matches plus 4 club_ratings calls per request
rivalry.tsx tab labels count only rated wins ('Singles (N)'), not total meetings; unrated meetings are listed but not counted
email-preview.tsx sends user_id '' for 'Preview as me'; the backend treats it as falsy, which works but is fragile

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all flows pass; 1 display defect in rivalry score orientation)

test_credentials: From /app/memory/test_credentials.md: alex+clerk_test@example.com (player), blair+clerk_test@example.com (admin), signed in with tickets from tests/_mint_tickets.py
seed_data_creation: Created preview challenges. Alex->Blair challenges: 1 declined, 1 cancelled, 1 completed and finalized as a real rated match (Blair won 6-4 6-3; Alex 7.92->7.72, Blair 6.08->6.28). Alex->player7: cancelled. No open challenges remain. Alex's monthly_digest was restored to false.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tickets are single-use and the browser session does not carry over between browser_automation runs, so re-run _mint_tickets.py before each run. Alex (7.72) and Blair (6.28) are NOT within each other's fair match range (max spread 1.0), so create an Alex->Blair challenge via POST /api/v1/clubs/{club}/challenges and then test Blair's side in the UI. The challenge form submit button is named 'Send challenge to <name>' (no type=submit). Accept/Decline/Cancel data-testids are on a span inside the button. The test email rate limit is 1 minute, stored in the DB (last_test_email_at). PUT /players/me is a full replace: send the existing profile fields along with any preference change.
rca of the issue: Rivalry score orientation: in head_to_head(), score_text is copied from RatedMatch as-is (side_one perspective) while a_side can be 2. rivalry.tsx renders A on the left with that raw score. Repro: open /players/<alex>/vs/<blair>; the top row shows 'Alex Tester 6-4 6-3 Blair Tester' with Blair bold. Fix: when a_side==2, reverse each set token (e.g. '6-4 6-3' -> '4-6 3-6', handling tiebreak notation) before returning, or flip it in the frontend.
